btlj.org.notes: recto running head is `<year>] <ARTICLE TITLE> <page>`; verso is `<page> <JOURNAL NAME> [Vol. N]` and is deliberately not matched (unmatched pages inherit). Pattern 1 requires the key to start with a non-digit and be <=59 chars so head-only-page-number heads and head-merged-into-body lines fail rather than producing junk keys. Pattern 2 recovers the ALL-CAPS title when the extractor glued the head onto the first body line. Boundaries land on the article's 2nd printed page (the opening page carries the display title, not the running head), so consumers should expect a 1-2 page lag. Volumes 1-9 (published as HIGH TECHNOLOGY LAW JOURNAL) use a bare `TITLE <page>` head with heavy OCR noise; those files match nothing and are left unsplit, which is the safe outcome. Many btlj.org files (e.g. `04-elazari-web.pdf`, `23-berkeley-tech-l-j-1141-1226.pdf`) are single articles, not compilations; the pattern yields one key for those. | back_off calibrated 2026-08-07 against the 4 largest deduped issues per domain: the default of 1 passed strictly fewer of them. Recto-only heads cycle over two pages, so the key first changes on the article third page.

journals.law.harvard.edu.notes: Domain hosts several Harvard journals; the splittable ones are Harvard Journal of Law & Public Policy full issues. Three recto head forms coexist across volumes: `No. 1] <Title> <page>` (vols 40-42), `2023 <Title> <page>` (vol 46), and a bare Title-Case `<Title>` line with the `No. 2]` marker landing on the page's LAST line (vols 31-33). Verso is `<page> Harvard Journal of Law & Public Policy [Vol. N]` and is excluded by the negative lookaheads. Pattern 3 requires >=3 lowercase letters and no digits so that ALL-CAPS display titles on article opening pages do NOT match (matching them would create 1-page phantom articles). Volume 47+ `-combined.pdf` files extract as one giant blob line and match nothing (left unsplit). `hlc-*` (Civil Rights-Civil Liberties) files are single articles. | back_off calibrated 2026-08-07 against the 4 largest deduped issues per domain: the default of 1 passed strictly fewer of them. Recto-only heads cycle over two pages, so the key first changes on the article third page.

administrativelawreview.org.notes: Head is the Word production slug, not a title. Pattern 3 catches the editor-in-chief variant `AUTHOR EIC REVIEW` / `AUTHOR-EIC REVIEW`, which is the same article as its numbered sibling; capturing only the surname unifies them and avoids a spurious boundary. Boundary pages land exactly on article opening pages.

cdr.creighton.edu.notes: Creighton Law Review. Recto head is the ALL-CAPS article/case-name title (sometimes prefixed `2005]`), verso is `CREIGHTON LAW REVIEW [Vol. N]`. Capturing only the FIRST word of the title is OCR-stable and gave exactly the right article count. Trade-off: two articles in the same issue whose titles share a first word would be merged. | back_off calibrated 2026-08-07 against the 4 largest deduped issues per domain: the default of 1 passed strictly fewer of them. www.atlanticlawjournal.org.notes: Atlantic Law Journal. Recto head is the ALL-CAPS article title (only its first line when the title wraps, which is fine because it is constant within an article); verso head is `ATLANTIC LAW JOURNAL, VOLUME N` and is excluded by the lookahead. The lookahead uses the trailing comma so that the real article `ATLANTIC LAW JOURNAL: TWENTY YEAR REVIEW` still matches. Front matter (EDITORS' CORNER, EDITORIAL BOARD) produces its own short runs, which is correct behaviour for this journal.

cjca.queenslaw.ca.notes: Canadian Journal of Commercial Arbitration. One 1-page table-of-contents page carries its own timestamp and splits the last article in two. | back_off calibrated 2026-08-07 against the 4 largest deduped issues per domain: the default of 1 passed strictly fewer of them. houstonlawreview.org.notes: Head is `Do Not Delete  <date>  <time>` with no author or title at all; the timestamp is the only per-article token. HH:MM only for the same whitespace reason as cilj. albertalawreview.com.notes: Files are per-article PDFs (133pp article at printed pages 734-866). www.aallnet.org.notes: Law Library Journal (AALL). The running head carries an explicit per-article production id in brackets -- `528 LAW LIBRARY JOURNAL Vol. 103:4 [2011-34]` on verso, `529BUILDING A COLLABORATIVE DIGITAL COLLECTIONVol. 103:4 [2011-34]` on recto -- so the key is the id itself: constant within an article, incremented between articles, and free of title/folio/OCR noise. Crucially the article's OWN first page carries only the bare folio (`527`) and no id, so the key first changes on the article's second page and the consumer's one-page back-off lands exactly on the display-title page. Every boundary inspected showed folio + head + display title. Only the id-bearing era splits: from roughly vol 107 onward LLJ dropped the running head entirely (first line is a bare folio, no head anywhere on the page), and those issues correctly return `no_running_head_signal` rather than a wrong split. On the AALL Spectrum question: this domain does host Spectrum material, but the >=20pp PDFs in the corpus are LLJ full issues plus a handful of AALL committee reports (`authenfinalreport.pdf`, `complete-fnb-021811.pdf`, `2009aallauthenticationreportupdates-2.pdf`); the Spectrum files present are one-page editor/calendar administrivia, not magazine issues. The reports match nothing and are left unsplit, which is the right outcome. 9 of 35 deduped candidate issues clear the validator; the other 26 are the headless later volumes or non-journal reports.

nulawreview.org.notes: Northeastern University Law Review. The per-article token lives on the VERSO head, which is `<folio>  <AuthorSurname>` (`2  Bessler`, `388 Meyer`, `384 Pack, Baker & Heere`); the recto head is `<folio>Vol. 13, Iss. 2 Northeastern University Law Review` with no space after the folio, so the mandatory `\s+` after the digits already excludes it and the `VOL|NOR|Vol` lookahead is belt-and-braces against the letter-spaced OCR variants (`NOR THEASTERN`). Roman-numeral front matter (`ii`, `iv`) does not match. Because the article's display-title page is a recto (journal-name head) and the author head first appears on the following verso, the key changes at page 2 of the article and the one-page back-off lands on the title page -- verified by eye on six issues, where every boundary page reads folio / journal name / display title. KNOWN LIMITS. (1) The first article of an issue never gets its own boundary: its author key is the first key seen, so no change is recorded and the consumer's synthetic start at page 1 absorbs front matter plus article one. (2) Parity is not uniform. When an article instead opens on a verso, or opens with a near-blank filler page that already carries the head (`388 Meyer`, with the real title page at 389), the key changes ON the opening page and the boundary lands one page early, on the previous article's last page. That is what sinks `volume-13-issue-2-book.pdf` (0.25) and `volume-12-issue-1.pdf` (0.43); `volume-13-issue-1-full-pdf.pdf` passes overall but two of its five boundaries land on a `ConClusion` page one page short. Measured across the 19 deduped candidates: 11 clear the validator, 6 fail it (and are correctly discarded), 2 never reach the rule. Of ~30 boundaries hand-checked, 3 were one page early. (3) Two articles by the same author in one issue would merge.

yalelawjournal.org.notes: NOT an issue-compilation domain. YLJ publishes per-article PDFs (`133-4-crumfinaldraft-jg6vf9cw-2.pdf`, `134-1-fletcher-...`, `zhangyljforumessay-...`), and the overwhelming majority of the 4,010 files scraped from this host are third-party documents the journal LINKS to from its footnotes: public laws (`plaw-111publ148.pdf`), congressional reports (`crpt-116hrpt346.pdf`), agency and NGO reports (`worldenergyoutlook2024.pdf`, `ipcc-ar6-syr-fullvolume.pdf`, `norc-2020-cocoa-report-english.pdf`), court filings, and city plans. Every one of the 63 deduped skip-manifest candidates for this domain is one of those third-party documents; none is a Yale Law Journal issue. There is no per-journal running head to find, and splitting a UN or GAO report on a law-review head pattern would be actively harmful, so the domain is marked single_article_domain to keep the splitter away from it. Any future pattern work here should first filter to `1NN-N-<author>-*.pdf` filenames, which are single articles anyway.

www.cschs.org.notes: INERT ENTRY - keys are excellent, boundaries are one page late on every article. California Legal History (California Supreme Court Historical Society). Recto head is `✯ <ARTICLE TITLE> <page>`; verso is `<page> CALIFORNIA LEGAL HISTORY ✯ VOLUME 17, 2022`, excluded by anchoring on the leading star. The pattern produced clean, correct, one-per-article keys on every volume tried - 21 for `legal-hist-v-17-2022.pdf` (676pp) and 15 for `legal-hist-v-15-2020.pdf` (684pp), including the multi-part `FOREWORD / PREFACE / CODA / BIBLIOGRAPHY: A SOCIAL HISTORY OF FARM LABOR IN CALIFORNIA` sequence. But articles open on rectos with a display title and NO running head (verified: p17 of v-17 opens `THE COMMUNITY JUSTICE / CLINIC: / Pepperdine Caruso School of Law`), the head resumes two pages later on p19, and the framework's fixed one-page back-off therefore emits p18 - a verso whose body resumes in mid-sentence. Opening share came out 0.20 / 0.29 / 0.33 / 0.29 across four volumes, so every document is discarded. Enable only with a two-page back-off. | ENABLED 2026-08-07 with back_off=2 after verifying boundaries land on display-title pages (cschs: 20 articles in a 676pp volume; columbia: 3). The recto-only head means the key first appears two pages after the opening.

journals.library.columbia.edu.notes: INERT ENTRY, and weak coverage even if the back-off were fixed. The splittable files here are scanned Columbia Business Law Review volumes whose running head sits on the page's LAST extracted line in the form `No. 3:637] 10(b) OR NOT 10(b)?`, where `637` is the article's printed START page - a per-article token that beats the OCR-mangled title (`I O(b) OR NOT IO(b)?`, `N 0(b)`). Capturing the title itself shreds into phantom runs; capturing the start page works: `28-2004columbuslrev637-2004.pdf` (262pp, printed 637 onwards) resolves to exactly four articles at 637 / 721 / 773 / 849. Two problems. (1) The closing bracket is frequently OCR'd as `1`, turning `637]` into `6371`, which is why the key is pinned to exactly three digits - fragile for any volume with 2- or 4-digit start pages. (2) Opening share was 0.50, and two of the three sampled scans (`21-2007columbuslrev614-2007.pdf`, `04-2008columbuslrev1-2008.pdf`) match nothing at all. Most files on this multi-journal domain are per-article (`07-2003columbuslrev35-2003.pdf` is one 156pp article). Not enabled. | ENABLED 2026-08-07 with back_off=2 after verifying boundaries land on display-title pages (cschs: 20 articles in a 676pp volume; columbia: 3). The recto-only head means the key first appears two pages after the opening.

www.texenrls.org.notes: Texas Environmental Law Journal. Recto head is `<year>] <Short Title> <page>` with an optional split year (`2009/2010] Solid Waste Update 3`); verso is `<page> TEXAS ENVIRONMENTAL LAW JOURNAL [VOL. 49:2]` and is not matched. Textbook recto-only style: every article opens on a recto display page carrying no head at all, so backoff 2 is required. With it, all four sampled issues score 1.00 and every boundary page verified by eye is a display title (`ADDRESSING B LURRED L INES: / INSTITUTIONAL D ESIGN S OLUTIONS TO`, `PFAS: U BIQUITOUS AND P ERSISTENT`, and so on; the extractor letter-spaces the small-cap initial but consistently). With the current backoff 1 the same rule scores 0.14-0.57 on eight of nine issues and the ninth emits boundaries one page late. NOT SPLITTABLE ON THIS DOMAIN: the recent `telj-NNnN-text-low.pdf` production series has no text-layer running head whatsoever - the first line of every page is the bare folio - and `telj53-1-2.pdf` is the same; those match nothing and are left unsplit.

loynolawreview.org.notes: Loyola Law Review. Full issues carry the Word production slug `(3) GARVEY.DOCX (DO NOT DELETE) 3/12/25 6:14 AM` as the first line of EVERY page, the article's opening page included, so the key changes on the opening page itself and the back-off must be ZERO - the opposite of the recto-title journals above. The key is the author surname taken from the `(n) SURNAME` prefix; capturing only that leading token matters because some slugs carry a date inside the filename (`(2) FIGUEROA 2.16.25.DOCX`), and an earlier pattern that required the whole stem to be alphabetic silently swallowed that article into the previous one. With backoff 0, `llr-711-full-issue-archive-12.pdf` yields 7 articles at 1.00 and every boundary is the display-title page (`(4) DACULA.DOCX ... // 123 // JUDGMENT DELAYED, JUSTICE DENIED:`). Under the current backoff 1 it scores 0.29 and is discarded. Most other files on the domain are per-article PDFs (`duval-daley-final-10-20-16.pdf`, the `61-2-*` series). The `2024] <Title> <page>` head that would suit backoff 1 sits on the page's SECOND line, which `_candidate_head_lines` cannot reach.
